title: Becoming a UGC Creator: How to Get Paid
summary: Learn how to build a UGC portfolio, read briefs, price by scope and rights, disclose partnerships, pitch brands, deliver work, and measure results.
body_markdown:
## Read the brief, rights, and pricing factors


### Turn a loose request into a written scope


Before quoting, clarify the number and format of assets, aspect ratio, duration, raw footage, hooks or variants, platform, posting requirement, product shipping, due date, review process, and expected revisions. Ask who supplies the script, substantiation for product claims, music, logos, and mandatory language. Confirm who approves the final version.


### Separate production from usage rights


Usage rights define where, how, and for how long a brand may use your work. Clarify organic social use, paid media, creator-handle advertising, websites, email, retail, territories, term, editing rights, sublicensing, and renewal. Exclusivity can also limit which competitors you may work with. Broad or long-lasting rights carry more value and responsibility than a limited organic placement, so they should not be treated as an afterthought.


### Price the factors, not an invented universal rate


There is no reliable rate that applies to every beginner or every market. Build a quote from production time, complexity, props or travel, number of deliverables, variants, revisions, turnaround, usage rights, exclusivity, posting, and administrative work. State what is included and how additional work will be approved. For payment, agree on currency, invoicing details, due date, cancellation terms, expenses, and any deposit or milestone structure appropriate to the project.


A contract should also cover ownership of raw files, permitted edits, reshoots, confidentiality, product returns, credit, termination, and the process for extending a license. If a clause is unclear or materially affects your rights, get qualified advice for your jurisdiction before accepting it.
